title: Ticagrelor (Brilinta)
keyNumbers: Stop 5 days before surgery with major bleeding risk when possible (label)

Ticagrelor + aspirin — noncardioembolic minor stroke (NIHSS ≤5) or high-risk TIA (ABCD2 ≥6, or symptomatic ≥50% intracranial/extracranial stenosis that could account for the TIA), <24 h, no IVT (THALES): 180 mg load, then 90 mg BID for up to 30 days; first maintenance dose 6–12 h after the load; with aspirin 300–325 mg load then 75–100 mg daily

Ticagrelor + aspirin — CYP2C19 loss-of-function carrier, minor stroke (NIHSS ≤3) or TIA (ABCD2 ≥4), <24 h, no IVT (CHANCE-2): 180 mg load, then 90 mg BID with aspirin × 21 days, then ticagrelor monotherapy
Aspirin maintenance >100 mg reduces effectiveness — keep 75–100 mg (label)
mechanism: Reversibly blocks P2Y12; no metabolic activation needed (CYP2C19-independent)

uses.agent: Ticagrelor + aspirin — noncardioembolic minor stroke (NIHSS ≤5) or high-risk TIA (ABCD2 ≥6, or symptomatic ≥50% intracranial/extracranial stenosis that could account for the TIA), <24 h, no IVT (THALES)
uses.doseText: 180 mg load, then 90 mg BID for up to 30 days; first maintenance dose 6–12 h after the load; with aspirin 300–325 mg load then 75–100 mg daily
notes: FDA-labeled stroke indication (NIHSS ≤5 or high-risk TIA)
evidenceNote: Kleindorfer 2021 §5.19 Rec 4: COR 2b, LOE B-R (SR) — ≥30% stenosis of an artery that could account for the event (THALES and AHA 2026: ≥50%)

uses.agent: Ticagrelor + aspirin — CYP2C19 loss-of-function carrier, minor stroke (NIHSS ≤3) or TIA (ABCD2 ≥4), <24 h, no IVT (CHANCE-2)
uses.doseText: 180 mg load, then 90 mg BID with aspirin × 21 days, then ticagrelor monotherapy
notes: May be reasonable instead of clopidogrel + aspirin in carriers

uses.doseText: Not recommended over aspirin (unstructured: recommendation against)
evidenceNote: AHA 2026: COR 3: No Benefit, LOE B-R

uses.agent: Ticagrelor — minor stroke/high-risk TIA <24 h with ipsilateral >30% intracranial stenosis
uses.doseText: 90 mg BID added to aspirin for up to 30 days (unstructured: see ICAD entry)

renalHepatic: No renal adjustment; ESRD on hemodialysis: exposure ~38% higher on non-dialysis days (label)
Severe hepatic impairment: exposure likely increased (label)

holdBeforeProcedure: Stop 5 days before surgery with major bleeding risk when possible (label)
thrombolysisRule: Prior SAPT/DAPT doesn't exclude IVT — give if otherwise eligible (AHA 2026 §4.6.1 Rec 9: COR 1, B-NR); sICH +0.9% SAPT / +1.2% DAPT absolute (class-level statement; agent not named)

reversal.doseText: Did not reverse ticagrelor in healthy volunteers; unlikely to help (unstructured: label statement)

evidenceNote: NCS 2016: suggestion for ADP-receptor inhibitor ICH

interactions: Avoid strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, clarithromycin, nefazodone) and strong inducers (rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital) (label)
Aspirin maintenance >100 mg reduces effectiveness — keep 75–100 mg (label)
pregnancy: Crosses the placenta; minimal pregnancy and lactation data (Miller 2026)
pearls: Contraindicated with any history of intracranial hemorrhage (label)
Tablets can be crushed and given in water orally or by NG tube (label)
Can cause false-negative platelet function tests for HIT; PF4 antibody testing unaffected (label)
After IVT: antiplatelets in the first 24 h might be considered only with a compelling indication (AHA 2026: COR 2b, B-NR); usual practice is 24-h imaging first
